The technology race with the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) is not one the United States can afford to lose. The national security threat that DeepSeek—a CCP-affiliated company—poses to the United States is alarming. DeepSeek's generative AI program acquires the data of U.S. users and stores the information for unidentified use by the CCP.

statements.text:
American leadership in Al is critical. Whoever is the leader in AI will dominate future warfare capabilities, cybersecurity, and wield unwavering economic influence.

The Chips Security Act will prevent the CCP from exploiting American technology to support programs like DeepSeek that threaten US national security.

The CCP has a track record of exploiting American technology to beat the U.S. militarily, diplomatically, and economically.

Under no circumstances should an American AI chip company support our foremost adversary. Congress must pass the Chip Security Act to prevent this.

The Chinese Communist Party is aggressively targeting the United States' advanced AI technology to undermine our national security. As AI becomes an integrated part of society, Congress must ensure that the United States fortifies our technology defenses and remains the undeniable leader.
statements.venue: Press release on Advanced AI Security Readiness Act

statements.text: AI is the next frontier on that. We lead the world in technology. We lead the world when it comes to AI.

Whoever wins this race in the future, it's going to be critical to future warfare capabilities, to, obviously, cybersecurity. And then, whoever wins the AI competition is going to yield really unwavering economic influence in the future.
As we look at, 'How do we win the strategic competition?' I think most experts would say we're ahead in AI right now against China, but not by much. It is a short lead,

We have to make sure that we are protecting this country appropriately, but also, it's equally important in making sure we win the strategic competition against China when it comes to AI, when it comes to quantum [and] when it comes to high-capacity chip manufacturing,
I'm real concerned about slowing down the innovation that we need in AI. If it was five years, I'd probably be happier with that, but I think some type of moratorium is a good thing.

The CCP continues to abide by a different set of rules and standards than the rest of the world. They steal intellectual property and technology, use coercive trade tactics, and weaponize cybersecurity to undermine national security.

AI is the next frontier, and we must be prepared.

The authoritarian CCP is engaged in a high-priority, coordinated AI campaign.

I'm proud to join my colleagues in introducing the No Adversarial AI Act. This bipartisan, bicameral bill constrains the CCP's access to sensitive U.S. government information. https://t.co/QWkzpVkd8Q

statements.text:
It was great to host this year’s winner and runner-up of the #IL16 Congressional App Challenge in my Peoria office and present them with a Certificate of Special Congressional Recognition!

The winning app “MeloCognia” uses AI to help detect Parkinson’s in its early stages and the second-place app “FENIX” helps healthcare personnel improve diagnosis and treatment times of patients.

Grateful to all the students who participated and made this year’s @CongressionalAC a success!

We need to win when it comes to AI. We need to win when it comes to quantum [computing]. That is the future for our country. [...] I think you've got to do it in a smart way. AI has so much promise, but there's also peril there. Finding that appropriate balance is, I think, the way we ought to look at that—but always remembering we have to win the strategic competition against China.
You need computer power to do that. Which is directly tied to data centers. Misinformation benefits our foreign competitors.

statements.text: I don't believe Washington should smother that with a heavy-handed regulatory regime. However, there is a real federal role: setting clear standards around AI safety and best practices, safeguarding Americans' data and security, and making sure bad actors like China can't steal the technology we're building here.

The approach that I take is, if the industry can self-regulate, if any industry can self-regulate, we ought to allow them to do that. If they cannot properly regulate than government needs to step in. I don't know if we are at that point yet but I do think we have to think about guidelines to protect our citizens, structures that can be put in place to make sure AI is not hurting people, particularly children and elderly people, vulnerable people in our society.
In PRC hands, this technology could be used to train military AI systems, accelerate cyber operations against U.S. networks, and expand state surveillance.
